nodes.name: Unbiased Estimator Condition
nodes.latex: E[\hat{\theta}] = \theta \quad \forall \ \theta \in \Theta
nodes.conditions: Holds for all possible values of parameter theta in parameter space Theta
nodes.description: An estimator whose mathematical expectation equals the true unknown parameter value.

nodes.name: Minimum Variance Unbiased Estimator (MVUE)
nodes.latex: \operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta}) \le \operatorname{Var}(\tilde{\theta}) \quad \forall \ \theta, \ \forall \ \tilde{\theta} \text{ such that } E[\tilde{\theta}] = \theta
nodes.conditions: Unbiased estimator with uniformly minimum variance across all allowable values of theta
nodes.description: Optimal estimator in MSE sense among the class of all unbiased estimators.

nodes.name: Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (Scalar Parameter)
nodes.latex: \operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta}) \ge \frac{1}{I(\theta)}, \quad I(\theta) = -E\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ln p(x; \theta)}{\partial \theta^2}\right] = E\left[\left(\frac{\partial \ln p(x; \theta)}{\partial \theta}\right)^2\right]
nodes.conditions: Assumes regularity condition E[d ln p / d theta] = 0; hat(theta) is unbiased
nodes.description: Fundamental theoretical lower bound on the variance of any unbiased estimator.

nodes.name: Fisher Information for i.i.d. Observations
nodes.latex: I(\theta) = N \cdot i(\theta) = -N E\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ln p(x[n]; \theta)}{\partial \theta^2}\right]
nodes.conditions: Observations x[0], ..., x[N-1] are independent and identically distributed
nodes.description: Fisher information scales linearly with sample size N under independent observations.

nodes.name: Vector Parameter CRLB (Covariance Matrix Inequality)
nodes.latex: \operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \ge I^{-1}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) \implies \operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta}_i) \ge [I^{-1}(\boldsymbol{\theta})]_{ii}
nodes.conditions: Matrix inequality: Cov(hat(theta)) - I^{-1}(theta) is positive semidefinite
nodes.description: Lower bound on the covariance matrix of an unbiased vector parameter estimator.

nodes.name: General Gaussian CRLB (Slepian-Bangs Formula)
nodes.latex: I(\theta) = \left[\frac{\partial \mu(\theta)}{\partial \theta}\right]^\top C^{-1}(\theta) \left[\frac{\partial \mu(\theta)}{\partial \theta}\right] + \frac{1}{2} \operatorname{Tr}\left[C^{-1}(\theta)\frac{\partial C(\theta)}{\partial \theta}C^{-1}(\theta)\frac{\partial C(\theta)}{\partial \theta}\right]
nodes.conditions: x \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu(\theta), C(\theta)); general Gaussian data with parameter-dependent mean and covariance
nodes.description: Evaluates Fisher information when both mean vector and covariance matrix depend on unknown parameter theta.

nodes.name: General Linear Model MVUE and CRLB
nodes.latex: \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} = (H^T C^{-1} H)^{-1} H^T C^{-1} x, \quad \operatorname{Cov}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) = (H^T C^{-1} H)^{-1} = I^{-1}(\boldsymbol{\theta})
nodes.conditions: Observation model x = H theta + w, where w ~ N(0, C) and H has full column rank
nodes.description: Exact MVUE and CRLB achiever for linear observation models under Gaussian noise.

nodes.name: Neyman-Fisher Factorization Theorem
nodes.latex: p(x; \theta) = g(T(x), \theta) \cdot h(x) \iff T(x) \text{ is a sufficient statistic for } \theta
nodes.conditions: g depends on x only through summary statistic T(x); h(x) is completely independent of theta
nodes.description: Core criterion establishing that data reduction via T(x) loses no information about parameter theta.

nodes.name: Rao-Blackwell Theorem
nodes.latex: \check{\theta} = E[\hat{\theta} \mid T(x)] \implies E[\check{\theta}] = \theta, \quad \operatorname{Var}(\check{\theta}) \le \operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta})
nodes.conditions: T(x) is sufficient statistic; strict inequality holds unless hat(theta) is already a function of T(x)
nodes.description: Conditioning any crude unbiased estimator on a sufficient statistic strictly improves or preserves variance.

nodes.name: Scalar Best Linear Unbiased Estimator (BLUE)
nodes.latex: \hat{\theta} = \frac{\mathbf{s}^\top C^{-1} \mathbf{x}}{\mathbf{s}^\top C^{-1} \mathbf{s}}, \quad \operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta}) = \frac{1}{\mathbf{s}^\top C^{-1} \mathbf{s}}
nodes.conditions: Linear observation model x = s theta + w with zero-mean noise w having covariance matrix C
nodes.description: Minimum variance linear unbiased estimator without requiring Gaussian or distributional noise assumptions.

nodes.name: Vector Best Linear Unbiased Estimator (Gauss-Markov)
nodes.latex: \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} = (H^\top C^{-1} H)^{-1} H^\top C^{-1} x, \quad C_{\hat{\theta}} = (H^\top C^{-1} H)^{-1}
nodes.conditions: Vector observation model x = H theta + w, where E[w] = 0 and Cov(w) = C; H has full column rank
nodes.description: Vector Best Linear Unbiased Estimator minimizing covariance for linear observation models.

nodes.name: Maximum Likelihood Estimator (MLE)
nodes.latex: \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{MLE}} = \arg\max_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} p(x; \boldsymbol{\theta}) = \arg\max_{\boldsymbol{\theta}} \ln p(x; \boldsymbol{\theta})
nodes.conditions: Log-likelihood is maximized over allowable parameter space Theta
nodes.description: Estimates parameter by choosing the value that maximizes the probability of observing the given dataset.

nodes.name: Asymptotic Normality and Efficiency of MLE
nodes.latex: \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{MLE}} \xrightarrow{a} \mathcal{N}\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}, I^{-1}(\boldsymbol{\theta})\right) \quad \text{as } N \to \infty
nodes.conditions: Under standard regularity conditions, MLE is asymptotically unbiased, asymptotically Gaussian, and asymptotically efficient (attains CRLB)
nodes.description: Asymptotic distribution of the Maximum Likelihood Estimator for large sample sizes.

nodes.name: Linear Least Squares Estimator (LSE)
nodes.latex: \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{LS}} = (H^\top H)^{-1} H^\top x, \quad J_{\min} = x^\top (I - H(H^\top H)^{-1} H^\top) x
nodes.conditions: H has full column rank; minimizes deterministic squared error criterion J = ||x - H theta||^2 with no statistical noise assumptions
nodes.description: Deterministic least squares parameter estimation based on projection onto the range of H.

nodes.name: Weighted Least Squares (WLS)
nodes.latex: \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{WLS}} = (H^\top W H)^{-1} H^\top W x, \quad J = (x - H\boldsymbol{\theta})^\top W (x - H\boldsymbol{\theta})
nodes.conditions: W is a symmetric positive definite weighting matrix
nodes.description: Least squares estimation with unequal weighting assigned to measurement errors.

nodes.name: Bayesian Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) - Posterior Mean
nodes.latex: \hat{\theta}_{\text{MMSE}} = E[\theta \mid x] = \int \theta p(\theta \mid x) d\theta
nodes.conditions: Minimizes Bayes risk under squared error loss function L(theta, hat(theta)) = (theta - hat(theta))^2
nodes.description: Optimal Bayesian estimator under squared error loss, given by the mean of the posterior probability density.

nodes.name: Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) Estimator
nodes.latex: \hat{\theta}_{\text{MAP}} = \arg\max_\theta p(\theta \mid x) = \arg\max_\theta [\ln p(x \mid \theta) + \ln p(\theta)]
nodes.conditions: Minimizes Bayes risk under hit-or-miss loss function L(theta, hat(theta)) = 0 if |theta - hat(theta)| < delta else 1 as delta -> 0
nodes.description: Bayesian point estimator choosing the mode (peak) of the posterior probability density function.

nodes.name: Linear Minimum Mean Square Error (LMMSE) Estimator
nodes.latex: \hat{\theta}_{\text{LMMSE}} = E[\theta] + C_{\theta x} C_{xx}^{-1} (x - E[x]), \quad \operatorname{Bmse}(\hat{\theta}) = \sigma_\theta^2 - C_{\theta x} C_{xx}^{-1} C_{x\theta}
nodes.conditions: Requires only knowledge of first and second moments (means and covariances), does not require complete PDFs
nodes.description: Best estimator constrained to be an affine function of observations x in the Bayesian MSE sense.

nodes.name: Kalman Filter State Measurement and Time Update
nodes.latex: \hat{s}[n \mid n] = \hat{s}[n \mid n-1] + K[n](x[n] - H[n]\hat{s}[n \mid n-1]), \quad \hat{s}[n \mid n-1] = A[n-1]\hat{s}[n-1 \mid n-1]
nodes.conditions: Linear dynamical state-space model: s[n] = A[n-1]s[n-1] + u[n], x[n] = H[n]s[n] + w[n]
nodes.description: Recursive MMSE state estimator update blending model prediction with new measurement innovation.

nodes.name: Kalman Gain and Error Covariance Update
nodes.latex: K[n] = M[n \mid n-1] H^\top[n] (C[n] + H[n] M[n \mid n-1] H^\top[n])^{-1}, \quad M[n \mid n] = (I - K[n] H[n]) M[n \mid n-1]
nodes.conditions: M[n|n-1] is predicted covariance matrix; M[n|n] is updated estimation error covariance matrix
nodes.description: Optimal time-varying gain weighting the innovation to minimize the posterior state error covariance.

nodes.name: MSE Bias-Variance Decomposition
nodes.latex: \operatorname{MSE}(\hat{\theta}) = E[(\hat{\theta} - \theta)^2] = \operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta}) + b^2(\hat{\theta}), \quad b(\hat{\theta}) = E[\hat{\theta}] - \theta
nodes.conditions: Holds for any estimator hat(theta) with finite second moment; b is estimator bias
nodes.description: Fundamental trade-off decomposing mean square estimation error into variance and squared bias.

nodes.name: CRLB Efficiency and Score Condition
nodes.latex: \frac{\partial \ln p(x; \theta)}{\partial \theta} = I(\theta)(\hat{\theta} - \theta) \iff \operatorname{Var}(\hat{\theta}) = \frac{1}{I(\theta)}
nodes.conditions: An unbiased estimator achieves the CRLB if and only if the score function is linear in hat(theta)
nodes.description: Necessary and sufficient condition for existence of an efficient unbiased estimator.

nodes.name: CRLB for Transformed Parameters
nodes.latex: \operatorname{Var}(\hat{g}(\theta)) \ge \frac{(g'(\theta))^2}{I(\theta)}, \quad g'(\theta) = \frac{\partial g(\theta)}{\partial \theta}
nodes.conditions: g(theta) is a differentiable function of parameter theta; hat(g) is an unbiased estimator of g(theta)
nodes.description: Lower bound on the variance of an unbiased estimator for a nonlinear function g(theta).

nodes.name: Vector Parameter Cramér-Rao Lower Bound
nodes.latex: C_{\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} - I^{-1}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) \ge 0, \quad [I(\boldsymbol{\theta})]_{ij} = -E\left[\frac{\partial^2 \ln p(x; \boldsymbol{\theta})}{\partial \theta_i \partial \theta_j}\right]
nodes.conditions: Matrix inequality: C_hat(theta) - I^-1(theta) is positive semi-definite; implies Var(hat(theta)_i) >= [I^-1(theta)]_ii
nodes.topic: Vector CRLB and Fisher Information Matrix
nodes.description: Matrix lower bound for multi-parameter unbiased estimation.

nodes.name: Fisher Information Matrix for Linear Gaussian Model
nodes.latex: I(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \frac{H^\top H}{\sigma^2}, \quad C_{\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}} \ge \sigma^2 (H^\top H)^{-1}
nodes.conditions: Observation model x = H theta + w, where w ~ N(0, sigma^2 I) and H has full column rank
nodes.description: Fisher information matrix and covariance bound for deterministic linear regression under Gaussian noise.

nodes.name: Lehmann-Scheffé Theorem (Unique MVUE)
nodes.latex: E[g(T(x))] = 0 \ \forall \theta \implies g(T) = 0 \ \text{a.e.} \implies \hat{\theta} = h(T(x)) \text{ is the UNIQUE MVUE}
nodes.conditions: T(x) is a complete sufficient statistic; unbiased function of complete sufficient statistic is unique MVUE
nodes.description: Guarantees that an unbiased estimator constructed from a complete sufficient statistic is the unique MVUE.

nodes.name: Likelihood Score Equation
nodes.latex: \left. \frac{\partial \ln p(x; \boldsymbol{\theta})}{\partial \boldsymbol{\theta}} \right|_{\boldsymbol{\theta} = \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{MLE}}} = \mathbf{0}
nodes.conditions: Necessary stationarity condition for interior local maxima of smooth log-likelihood functions
nodes.description: Stationary points of log-likelihood function where the gradient vanishes.

nodes.name: Invariance Property of Maximum Likelihood Estimators
nodes.latex: \widehat{g(\boldsymbol{\theta})}_{\text{MLE}} = g(\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{MLE}})
nodes.conditions: Holds for any function g, whether one-to-one or many-to-one (using induced likelihood)
nodes.description: Estimating a transformed parameter g(theta) is accomplished simply by plugging in the MLE of theta.

nodes.name: Least Squares Orthogonality Principle
nodes.latex: H^\top (x - H \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{LS}}) = \mathbf{0} \implies e \perp \operatorname{range}(H)
nodes.conditions: Error vector e = x - H hat(theta) is orthogonal to the subspace spanned by columns of H
nodes.description: Geometric foundation of least squares: minimal residual error occurs when error vector is perpendicular to signal subspace.

nodes.name: Method of Moments (MOM) Estimator
nodes.latex: \mu_k = E[x^k] = g_k(\theta_1, \dots, \theta_P), \quad \hat{\mu}_k = \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x^k[n] \implies \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}} = \mathbf{g}^{-1}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\mu}})
nodes.conditions: Equates sample moments to theoretical moments of the underlying probability distribution
nodes.description: Simple consistent estimation procedure equating empirical sample moments with theoretical distribution moments.

nodes.name: Bayesian Posterior Distribution
nodes.latex: p(\theta \mid x) = \frac{p(x \mid \theta) p(\theta)}{p(x)} = \frac{p(x \mid \theta) p(\theta)}{\int p(x \mid \theta) p(\theta) d\theta}
nodes.conditions: p(theta) is prior distribution; p(x|theta) is data likelihood; p(theta|x) is updated posterior
nodes.description: Core Bayesian formulation treating the unknown parameter theta as a random variable with prior uncertainty.

nodes.name: Gaussian Conjugate Prior Posterior Update
nodes.latex: x \sim \mathcal{N}(\theta, \sigma^2), \ \theta \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_\theta, \sigma_\theta^2) \implies p(\theta \mid x) = \mathcal{N}\left(\frac{\sigma^2 \mu_\theta + \sigma_\theta^2 x}{\sigma^2 + \sigma_\theta^2}, \frac{\sigma^2 \sigma_\theta^2}{\sigma^2 + \sigma_\theta^2}\right)
nodes.conditions: Conjugate Gaussian model where prior and posterior share the same functional normal family
nodes.description: Closed-form Gaussian Bayesian updating combining prior mean and observation into precision-weighted posterior mean.

nodes.name: Bayesian Absolute Error Estimator (Posterior Median)
nodes.latex: \int_{-\infty}^{\hat{\theta}_{\text{Med}}} p(\theta \mid x) d\theta = \frac{1}{2} \iff \hat{\theta}_{\text{Med}} = \operatorname{median}(\theta \mid x)
nodes.conditions: Minimizes Bayes risk under absolute error loss L(theta, hat(theta)) = |theta - hat(theta)|
nodes.description: Posterior median minimizing expected absolute deviation error.

nodes.name: Vector Linear MMSE Estimator
nodes.latex: \hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{\text{LMMSE}} = E[\boldsymbol{\theta}] + C_{\theta x} C_{xx}^{-1} (x - E[x]), \quad M_{\hat{\theta}} = C_{\theta\theta} - C_{\theta x} C_{xx}^{-1} C_{x\theta}
nodes.conditions: M_hat(theta) is Bayesian MSE error covariance matrix for multi-parameter vector theta
nodes.description: Multi-parameter linear Bayesian estimation optimal in trace covariance sense.

nodes.name: Non-Causal Wiener Filter Frequency Response
